<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Ubufox" /></noinclude><section begin=par136 />{{GHGpar-heading|136|The Demonstrative Pronoun}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|a}}
The ''demonstrative pronouns'' are {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} (§ 34), ''hic, haec'' (''hoc''), ''hi'', &c., and the personal pronoun {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, likewise used as a demonstrative, fem. {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}, plur. masc. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}} ({{GHGpar|32|b}}), ''is'', ''ea'' (''id''), or ''ille'', &c., ''ii'', ''eae'' or ''illi'', &c. The distinction between them in usage is that {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} (like ''hic'', ὅδε) almost always points out a (new) person or thing present, while {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} (like ''is'', ''ille'', αὐτός, ἐκεῖνος) refers to a person or thing already mentioned or known (see the examples below).<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} standing separately as determinate in themselves, see {{GHGpar|125|i}}. On the use of determinate demonstratives as adjectives, see {{GHGpar|126|u}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|b}}
Rem. 1. Compare the instructive examples in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=4}} ''of whom I say unto thee, this'' ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}) ''shall go with thee, he'' ({{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}) ''shall go with thee'' (so afterwards with negatives). Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה|translate=this day}}, i.e. the actual day on which one is speaking or writing ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=33}}, &c.), but {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם הַהוּא}} the day or period of which the historian has just been speaking ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=32|hidebook=1}}) or of which the prophet has just been foretelling ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, 20 ff.) and of which he continues to speak or foretell. Nevertheless {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} are also found in certain common combinations where {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} would be expected, and vice versa; thus almost always {{GHGheb|text=הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵ֫לֶּה}}, but {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵ֫מָּה}} or {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם}}—With a secondary sense of contempt (like Latin ''iste'') {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} occurs, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}, &c. In the sense of the neuter, ''this'', {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}} is more common than {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, &c., but {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} more common than {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|c}}
2. Both {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} are sometimes used almost as enclitics to emphasize interrogative words (like the Latin ''nam'' in ''quisnam''; cf. also ''quis tandem''); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=מִי זֶה|translate=who now}} (darkeneth, &c.)...? {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=55}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, &c; {{GHGheb|text=מַה־זֶּה|translate=what now?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=11}}; ''how now?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=20}}; ''why now?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=24}}; but before the verb {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}} it is usually {{GHGheb|text=מַה־זֹּאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה־זֶּה|translate=wherefore now?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=23}}, &c.—So also {{GHGheb|text=מִי־הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=7}} ff.; and still more emphatically {{GHGheb|text=מִי הוּא־זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|d}}
3. {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} is likewise used as an enclitic (see c above): (''a'') ''of place'', in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתָּה זֶה וגו׳|translate=whether thou}} (that art here) ''be my son Esau?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=20}} ''is it thou?'' {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה־זֶה|translate=behold, here}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=9}};<ref>On the other hand, it is very questionable whether {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה הַיָּם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה הָעָם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה סִינַי}}) can be taken, according to the common explanation, simply as a prefixed demonstrative particle (''the sea yonder'', &c.). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=הַיָּם}} may be in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}; cf. § 126 aa, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=7}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה אַחַת}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}} depending on {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}, and also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=45}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הַלִּשְׁכָּה}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֹה}}; otherwise it is most naturally taken as the subject, ''this is the sea''. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=14}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=9}} might also be explained in the same way; but in these passages the text is almost certainly corrupt. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}} in fact {{GHGheb|text=זֶה סִינַי}} is most probably to be regarded with Moore as a very early gloss, which subsequently found its way from this passage into Ps 68.</ref> cf. also the strengthen-<section end=par136 /><noinclude>
